newsitem.title: BOSNIA: OSCE probes voter registration fraud in Bosnia.
newsitem.headline: OSCE probes voter registration fraud in Bosnia.

text.p: The Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe said on Tuesday it was investigating reports of fraudulent voter registration in Bosnian Serb-controlled territory.

"I can assure you that we will continue to pursue our investigations with the utmost urgency and I predict that you will not have to wait too long before such results are made public," David Foley, spokesman for the OSCE, told reporters.

Foley declined to discuss details of an internal report by election supervisors which warned of attempts by Bosnian Serb authorities to orchestrate "massive fraud" in the country's upcoming municipal elections.

The report, leaked to the press on Monday, accused Serb authorities of trying to inflate the number of eligible Serb voters in contested areas which had a large Moslem population before the 1992-95 war.
The head of the OSCE mission in Bosnia. U.S. diplomat Robert Frowick, said the internal report proved that international supervisors were closely monitoring the registration process.

"The way this has happened shows the system is working because the OSCE has brought attention to the problem and the OSCE is acting to correct it with what I believe will certainly prove to be effective mechanisms," Frowick said.
The report said Bosnian Serb authorities, intent on sealing the results of wartime "ethnic cleansing", were forging identity papers for Serbs who fled their homes in neighbouring Croatia.
It also said authorities were coercing Serb refugees to register where they have resettled instead of the municipalities which now lie inside the country's Moslem-Croat federation.
Foley said if investigators confirmed that fraud had occurred, the OSCE had the authority to impose severe penalties -- including striking candidates from ballots.
The OSCE election appeals sub-commission was expected to examine the reports of fraud in Serb territory and deliver a ruling by the end of the week, Western officials said.
The officials, who asked not to be named, said the case provided the OSCE with an important test as to how it would treat authorities attempting to rig the municipal vote scheduled for September.
National elections held last September in Bosnia were marred by allegations of fraud and dubious voter lists.
